body:
## Recent Activity

Synced window: 2026-05-12T13:07:05Z to 2026-05-13T13:07:05Z. Signals include 14 issues, 13 PRs, 5 discussions, and 0 commits.

Activity centered on self-approval/self-merge follow-through, orchestrator route behavior, contextual `/implement` issue titles, and several design discussions about future orchestration modes.

## Recently Active PRs

- Merged: [#172](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/172), [#180](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/180), [#184](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/184), [#186](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/186), and [#219](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/219).
- Closed without merge: [#166](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/166), [#202](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/202), [#208](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/208), and [#214](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/214), largely superseded by split or simplified follow-up work.
- Open and recently reviewed: [#232](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/232) derives explicit `/implement` tracking issue titles from command text; [#235](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/235) adds opt-in self-merge after self-approval.
- Open and newly created: [#236](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/236) generates contextual titles for explicit implement issues.
- Still open from prior route-catalog work: [#221](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/221), with discussion favoring a more minimal shared route catalog.

## Recently Active Issues

- [#170](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/170) remains the main self-approval tracking issue; orchestration reported child [#229](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/229) completed with PR [#235](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/235) ready to ship.
- Closed child tasks: [#171](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/171), [#175](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/175), [#183](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/183), [#185](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/185), and [#218](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/218).
- [#119](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/119) was closed after “agent installation runtime” was added.
- New/open follow-ups include [#224](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/224) for requester-author self-approval blocking, [#227](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/227) for orchestrator small bugs/questions, [#228](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/228) for better implement issue names, [#231](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/231) for installation docs, [#233](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/233) for flexible Codex/Claude credential setup, and [#234](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/234) for contextual explicit implement metadata.

## Recently Active Discussions

- [#223](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/discussions/223) explored whether Sepo can support autoresearch-style iterative refinement; the visible answer identified a missing deterministic experiment/result state machine.
- [#225](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/discussions/225) proposed orchestrator sub-modes, reframed as orchestration strategy.
- [#226](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/discussions/226) covered parallel orchestrator subtasks and noted the current single-next-action invariant.
- [#230](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/discussions/230) discussed multi-repo meta-orchestration as a product direction, not current built-in behavior.
- [#222](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/discussions/222) is the prior daily summary and received a request to triage latest activity.

## Follow-ups

- Review and decide merge path for open PRs [#232](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/232), [#235](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/235), and [#236](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/236).
- Prioritize [#224](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/224), since it describes a policy gap in self-approval requester/author checks.
- Decide whether [#221](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/221) should be narrowed or superseded by a smaller route-catalog change.

@sepo-agent /answer 

Review all the issues and determine key user facing functions -- for example auto answer mode?

I reviewed the mirrored issue set and current docs. The key user-facing functions cluster into these product modes:

| Function | User-facing behavior | Status from issues |
|---|---|---|
| **Ask / Answer** | `@sepo-agent /answer` answers repo questions, explains code, and handles plan-only guidance. | Core route; planning behavior came from #10. |
| **Auto answer / implicit follow-up mode** | If an issue/PR is already agent-tagged and a user asks a follow-up but forgets `@sepo-agent`, Sepo can infer whether to answer or ignore. | Proposed in #124. I would name it `implicit follow-ups`, gated by something like `AGENT_IMPLICIT_FOLLOWUPS_ENABLED`. |
| **Implement** | `@sepo-agent /implement` creates a branch and PR for a requested change. Works from issues, PRs, and discussions via tracking issue when needed. | Core route; gaps around better tracking issue names in #228/#234. |
| **Review PR** | `@sepo-agent /review` runs AI review, synthesis, rubrics review, and current-head provenance. | Core route; lots of polish around collapsing stale reviews and inline review handling. |
| **Fix PR** | `@sepo-agent /fix-pr` updates an existing PR branch in response to review feedback. | Core route; status/comment cleanup covered by #68 and related issues. |
| **Orchestrate** | `@sepo-agent /orchestrate` runs bounded multi-step automation: implement, review, fix, delegate child issues, resume parent tasks, and stop/ask when blocked. | Major product surface from #19, #33, #76, #98, #101, #105, #170. |
| **Discussion coordination** | Use a discussion thread as a lightweight coordination/control surface while concrete work still happens through issues/PRs. | Proposed in #103; not the same as full discussion-based implementation orchestration. |
| **Self-approval** | After a trusted `SHIP` review, Sepo can approve its own PR when explicitly enabled. | Implemented behind `AGENT_ALLOW_SELF_APPROVE`; tracked in #170. |
| **Self-merge** | After trusted self-approval, Sepo can merge the PR when explicitly enabled and deterministic checks pass. | Implemented behind `AGENT_ALLOW_SELF_MERGE`; from #200/#213/#229/#235. |
| **Skills / custom actions** | `@sepo-agent /skill <name>` and `agent/s/<skill>` labels run repo-defined skills. `create-action` helps add durable scheduled workflows. | Core/extensibility surface; #201 says skill route needs more work. |
| **Onboarding / install / update** | Setup check creates labels and setup issue; update workflow checks for Sepo infra updates and opens/update PRs. | Important distribution surface from #23, #27, #94, #119, #212, #231. |
| **Memory and rubrics** | Agent remembers project context in `agent/memory`; rubrics capture user/team preferences in `agent/rubrics`. | Core differentiator; issues #2, #9, #93, #205, #238. |
| **Project management** | Scheduled/manual triage of open issues/PRs, priority/effort labels, daily summaries. | Exists but opt-in/dry-run by default; #34, #125, #126, #140, #142. |
| **Access / grant UX** | Maintainers can grant external users one-shot access to a specific request instead of globally widening permissions. | Designed in #31; important for public repos. |
| **Failure diagnosis/reporting** | Detect failed agent runs, diagnose, and optionally report issues back to GitHub. | Proposed/partially explored in #26 and #156. |

My recommended top-level user-facing framing:

1. **Ask**: answer questions and produce plans.  
2. **Change**: implement or fix code.  
3. **Review**: review PRs and apply rubrics.  
4. **Orchestrate**: run multi-step work with progress tracking.  
5. **Autopilot PRs**: optional self-approve and self-merge.  
6. **Remember**: memory and rubrics.  
7. **Maintain**: scheduled summaries, project management, updates, failure reporting.  
8. **Extend**: skills and custom actions.

For your example: yes, **auto answer mode** is a real user-facing function worth naming, but I would scope v1 narrowly: only on `agent`-labeled issues/PRs, only for unmentioned follow-up comments, only route to `answer` or `ignore`, and opt out via repo variable. That keeps it useful without accidentally launching implementation or orchestration from ambiguous comments.
